newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF mission to start new credit talks in Kiev.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to start new credit talks in Kiev.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission will discuss a new multi-billion dollar credit programme with Ukrainian officials when it visits the capital Kiev this week, the Fund's resident representative said on Monday.

Alex Sundakov said officials would look into the latest tranche of a stand-by loan which is due to expire next year, as well as discussing the possibility of a new Extended Fund Facility (EFF) loan programme.
"We'll be talking about the EFF and it's time for another review of the tranche," Sundakov said.
The latest mission is scheduled to begin its two-week visit on Tuesday for talks on the $2.5 to $3 billion EFF, which IMF officials have said could be agreed this year.
The programme would start in 1997 and succeed the $867 million stand-by loan, now being disbursed in monthly tranches.
The three-year programme would include a $1.5 billion currency stabilisation fund for the new hryvnia currency, introduced on September 2.
The hryvnia slipped to 1.793 on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Monday from 1.788 on Friday.
Fund missions have been visiting Ukraine almost monthly to review economic progress and approve monthly disbursements.
Ukraine has secured about $2.1 billion in IMF credits since winning approval for its market reform programme in 1994.

Its draft 1997 budget, aimed at meeting IMF guidelines, calls for inflation to slow to 24.9 percent from 48 percent forecast this year and a reduction in the budget deficit to 2.4 percent of gross domestic product by Western calculations.
Parliamentary deputies, set to begin reviewing the budget on November 5, have said the deficit figure is unrealistic.
